title: Creative Commons License Switches
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: A panel of three switches (Attribution, ShareAlike, NonCommercial) that shows how each Creative Commons element changes the license name and takes a freedom away from the person who receives the work. Attribution is always on.

learningObjectives: Explain how the ShareAlike and NonCommercial elements each narrow what a person receiving a Creative Commons work may do
Name the license that results from any setting of the Attribution, ShareAlike, and NonCommercial switches
Explain why the Attribution element is always on
prerequisites: The five R permissions (retain, reuse, revise, remix, redistribute)
Definitions of the Attribution, ShareAlike, and NonCommercial requirements

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, flip a switch, and observe the result
keyQuestions: Which freedom does NonCommercial take away?
Which freedom does ShareAlike take away?
Why can the Attribution switch never be turned off?
commonMisconceptions: NonCommercial only forbids selling the exact file
Attribution is optional when the work is shared for free
assessmentOpportunities: Name the license shown for each switch setting without looking
Choose which switches must be off for a stated reuse, such as selling printed copies

controls.name: Attribution (BY) switch
controls.description: Locked on. Clicking it explains that every Creative Commons license requires credit to the creator.

controls.name: ShareAlike (SA) switch
controls.description: Turns the ShareAlike requirement on or off. When on, picking the license for a remix is taken away.

controls.name: NonCommercial (NC) switch
controls.description: Turns the NonCommercial requirement on or off. When on, commercial use is taken away.
